items.headline: Yamamoto shoves, Freeman goes deep — Dodgers grab a 2-1 NLDS lead
items.body: The Dodgers flipped their series in Atlanta. Yoshinobu Yamamoto was electric — 10 strikeouts over seven innings — while Kiké Hernández launched a two-run homer and Freddie Freeman homered for a second straight game to back him up. Edwin Díaz slammed the door for a 3-1 Game 3 win, and L.A. now leads the Braves 2-1 with Game 4 tonight.
items.say: The Dodgers took the lead on the Braves last night — their Japanese ace struck out 10 and Freddie Freeman keeps hitting homers. They can basically take control tonight. You following any October baseball, or just the highlights?

items.headline: Padres live to fight another day — Cronenworth's homer beats the Brewers
items.body: Facing a sweep, San Diego punched back. Jake Cronenworth belted the go-ahead homer, Michael King slammed the back door with two innings of relief, and Xander Bogaerts turned a game-ending double play to seal a 4-3 win at Petco Park. The top-seeded Brewers still lead the series 2-1, but the Padres forced a Game 4 tonight with the season on the line.
items.say: The Padres were one loss from going home and won it on a late homer to stay alive. Win-or-go-home games are the best part of October. You got a team still in it, or just here for the drama?

items.headline: Two teams on the brink tonight — White Sox and Rays go for the finish
items.body: It's clinch-or-sweat night in the AL. The upstart White Sox host the favored Guardians up 2-0 and a win sends them to their first League Championship Series since their 2005 title run. Over in the Bronx, the top-seeded Rays also lead 2-0 and can bounce the Yankees out of October. Two Game 3s, two teams staring at elimination.
items.say: A couple of baseball teams could get knocked out of the playoffs tonight — the Yankees are on the ropes, and the White Sox are one win from their deepest run since 2005. You gotta love an elimination game. You catching any of it?

items.headline: Big draw, big absence — Shanghai Masters opens without world No. 1 Sinner
items.body: Tennis's fall swing rolls into China: the Rolex Shanghai Masters is underway (through Oct 18), but world No. 1 Jannik Sinner pulled out as he nurses the knee that's bugged him since Wimbledon. That cracks the door wide open — Carlos Alcaraz and Alexander Zverev headline as the top two seeds, with Zverev chasing the No. 1 ranking and Novak Djokovic lurking in the field.
items.say: The big Shanghai tennis tournament just started, and the No. 1 player pulled out hurt — so it's wide open for Alcaraz and the rest. Always fun when the favorites get shaken up. You follow tennis at all, or just the big Slams?

items.headline: Upset in Poland — underdog 1win crash the CS2 party and pocket $100K
items.body: The Counter-Strike playoff picture just got spicy. At ESL Pro League Season 24 in Katowice, scrappy underdog 1win stunned powerhouse Team Spirit 2-0 to punch their playoff ticket — and their owner reportedly tossed the team a $100K bonus for it. MOUZ and Vitality cruised in at 3-0, while fan-favorite G2 crashed out, snapping six straight major playoff runs. The Spodek Arena playoffs start Friday.
items.say: Big Counter-Strike tournament in Poland had a huge upset — a small underdog team beat one of the giants and their boss handed them a hundred grand. The arena playoffs start Friday. You ever watch any esports, or is it a total mystery to you?

items.headline: Taylor breaks the all-time record — 'The Life of a Showgirl' is a juggernaut
items.body: The numbers are bananas. Taylor Swift's 12th album, 'The Life of a Showgirl,' moved more than 4 million units in the U.S. in week one — the biggest sales week in recorded-music history, topping Adele's old mark. Every one of its 12 songs landed on the Billboard Hot 100 (a first), lead single 'The Fate of Ophelia' went straight to No. 1, and the splashy theater release party raked in another ~$33M at the box office.
items.say: Taylor Swift's new album just had the biggest sales week in history — like four million copies in seven days, and every song on it charted. Say what you want, the woman's a machine. You a Swiftie, or is she just always on in your house?

items.headline: Affleck goes dark — Netflix drops the kidnapping thriller 'Animals' Friday
items.body: Ben Affleck directs, co-writes and stars in 'Animals,' a tense R-rated thriller hitting Netflix (and some theaters) this Friday, Oct 9. He plays an L.A. mayoral hopeful whose world unravels when his son is kidnapped, forcing him and his wife (Kerry Washington) into some very ugly choices. Gillian Anderson and Steven Yeun round out a stacked cast. Think 'The Town' energy, cranked up.
items.say: There's a new Ben Affleck thriller on Netflix Friday — he directs and stars, playing a guy whose kid gets kidnapped and things spiral fast. Looks like a tense one. You into the gritty thriller stuff, or more of a comfort-watch person?

items.headline: Hadouken! — the big-budget 'Street Fighter' movie lands next week
items.body: Nostalgia alert for anyone who ever fed quarters into an arcade: a loud, star-packed live-action 'Street Fighter' hits theaters Oct 16. Jason Momoa, 50 Cent and wrestling stars Cody Rhodes and Roman Reigns join Andrew Koji's Ryu and the whole roster of iconic fighters for what looks like gleefully over-the-top, hand-to-hand chaos. Early reactions call it big, dumb and a lot of fun.
items.say: They made a new Street Fighter movie — Jason Momoa, 50 Cent, a couple of the WWE guys, the whole arcade crew. Looks ridiculous in the best way. You ever play the games growing up, or was that before your time?

items.headline: 'No alliance lasts forever' — 'The Diplomat' returns for Season 3
items.body: The addictive Netflix thriller is back: Season 3 of 'The Diplomat' drops Oct 16, with Keri Russell again as the reluctant, perpetually-flustered ambassador trying to keep the world from catching fire. Allison Janney and Bradley Whitford join the cast this year, and the Season 2 cliffhanger left a lot to untangle. Perfect prestige-binge fuel for a cozy fall weekend.
items.say: The Diplomat's coming back for a new season on Netflix next week — that tense, fast-talking show with Keri Russell. Great one to binge when it gets chilly out. You ever watch it, or need a new show for the fall?
